rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī glosses the fortunate as people who attain their aims and find their affairs made easy.
rows.anchor: أي فازوا بمطالبهم وتيسر أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is already a religious certainty, and the fortunate dwell there eternally.
rows.anchor: أي التي صارت معلومة من الدين بالضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fortunate remain in Paradise forever, without end.
rows.anchor: على ما جرت به عادة العرب في إرادة التأبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs use the heavens-and-earth formula idiomatically to express endless duration.
rows.anchor: على ما جرت به عادة العرب في إرادة التأبيد لا آخر بمثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated exception does not cancel eternal bliss; the following assurance that the gift is unsevered is its strongest proof.
rows.anchor: وأدل دليل على ما قلت في الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unsevered means neither cut off, broken, divided, nor diminished; even a momentary interruption would make the gift severed or reduced.
rows.anchor: اي مقطوع ولا مكسور ولا مفصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ending with the unsevered gift firmly establishes permanence and comforts Paradise's people, in contrast to the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي الختم بذلك من الجزم بالدوام طمأنينة لأهل الجنة زيادة في نعيمهم عكس ما كان لأهل النار

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī glosses zafīr as repeated voiced breathing and shahīq as a terrible prolonged inward sound; their roots suggest strain or length, while khālid means perpetual residence and dāʾim continuing duration.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الرماني : والزفير : ترديد النفس مع الصوت حتى تنتفخ الضلوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the two groups' final judgment strengthens the Prophet to carry out the whole mission, trusting God's support before the gathered people.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبره تعالى بوقوع القضاء بتمييز الناس في اليوم المشهود إلى القسمين المذكورين على الحكم المشروح مرهبا ومرغبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great stakes arouse suspense about the consequence, prompting a concise, forceful wording that quickly delivers the point.
rows.anchor: عظيم تشوف النفس وشديد شوقها لعلم ما سبب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn is deleted from kāna in tak to make the wording concise, hasten the answer, and intensify the denial of doubt.
rows.anchor: اقتضى ذلك حذف النون من ( كان ) إيجازا في الكلام للإسراع بالإيقاف على المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praised patience restrains the self from unlawful conduct, especially abandoning truth; its opposite is despair.
rows.anchor: والصبر المحمود : حبس النفس عن الخروج إلى ما لا يجوز من ترك الحق , ونقيضه الجزع

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet says patience has the better outcome, while without it events will unfold as the listeners already see.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : إن تصبر فالصبر خير مغبة وإن تجزعا فالأمر ما تريان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is bitter restraint from desire, supported by the honor and reward of obeying right, hope of good consequences, and habituation.
rows.anchor: فهو أكره شيء إلى النفس , والمعين عليه ما في استشعار لزوم الحق من العز والأجر بالطاعة

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī says ṣabr has become so associated with truth that it is scarcely used except in that sense.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز إطلاقه إلا فيه - قاله الرماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding stories show that stubborn opponents will not be persuaded by human intervention, that their worship is imitation, and that communities disputed over Moses' revealed guidance; this checks wishful hopes of accommodating them.
rows.anchor: وكان من طبع البشر البعد عن الانتهاء عن الخواطر إلا بعد التجربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the command to be patient in doing good and forbidding wrong, the verse answers the imagined objection by explaining why earlier peoples were destroyed.
rows.anchor: كان من الجائز أن يقع في فكر الاعتراض بأن يقال : ما الموجب لذلك

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī allows lولا here, as in Yūnus, to express either reproach or a question.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز إطلاقه إلا فيه - قاله الرماني

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows lولا as an exhortation directed to the present listener, urging people to forbid corruption.
rows.anchor: كما قال الزمخشري , ويكون للسامع لا للمهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation addresses listeners rather than the already destroyed: their fate strongly urges others to command right and warns them against repeating their conduct.
rows.anchor: لأن الآية لما تضمنت إهلاك المقر على الفساد كان في ذلك أقوى حث لغيرهم على الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generations meant are the previously mentioned destroyed peoples, powerful people from earlier periods.
rows.anchor: أي المهلكين الأشداء الكائنين في زمان ما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those of baqiyya are people possessing sound judgment, goodness, and vigilance about what benefits them.
rows.anchor: حفظ وخير ومراقبة لما يصلحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of baqiyya carries the associated ideas of gathering, strength, keeping or guarding, watching, endurance, and quality.
rows.anchor: لأن مادة ( بقي ) تدور على الجمع , ويلزمه القوة والثبات والحفظ

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains baqiyya as the best portion a person keeps back; one described as a remnant of a people is among their finest.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : لأن الرجل يستبقي مما يخرجه أجوده وافضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeatedly renew their prohibition of corruption, a phrasing that signals how many corruptors there were.
rows.anchor: في كل حين إشارة غلى كثرة المفسدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception denotes the few righteous people whom God saved; they were the ones who forbade corruption.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ( من ) بيانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is explanatory: those saved are the same people described as the few who forbade corruption.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ( من ) بيانية , اي هم الذين أنجينا فإنهم نهوا عن الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording anjaynā signals beneficial rescue that motivates opposition to corruption; using najjaynā would suggest gradual deliverance and distort the point.
rows.anchor: عبر بالإنجاء لأنه الدال على الخير الحامل للنهي عن الفساد دون التنجية الدالة على التدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority followed the path of wrongdoing, specifically by failing to forbid corruption; the unqualified wording broadens the description.
rows.anchor: أوقعوا الظلم بترك النهي عن الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording focuses on the luxury bestowed on them: affluence made them arrogant and tyrannical.
rows.anchor: فأبطرتهم النعمة حتى طغوا وتجبروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were entrenched criminals; their crime is a persistent severing of God's bond.
rows.anchor: أي متصفين على سبيل الرسوخ بالإجرام , وهو قطع حبل الله على الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed them for their entrenched crimes; absent their criminality, destruction would count as injustice by ordinary standards.
rows.anchor: فإن إهلاكهم على تقدير الانفكاك عن الإجرام يكون ظلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, whose attribute here signals beneficence, does not destroy towns unjustly while their people are genuinely reforming, though He is not answerable for His acts.
rows.anchor: ذكر سبحانه بالوصف المفهم للإحسان تثبيتا له وتأمينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rules out a town-wide destruction as misplaced while its inhabitants are deeply engaged in reform, whether the injustice were small or great.
rows.anchor: أي أي ظلم كان , صغير أو كبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction is making sensation cease; a thing is destroyed when it becomes lost so its location is unknown, while reform makes affairs sound as reason requires.
rows.anchor: والإهلاك : إيجاب ما يبطل الإحساس , والهالك : ضياع الشيء وهو حصوله بحيث لا يدري اين هو

words: لَوْلَآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَةٌۭ مِّن رَّبِّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers mock God's power by demanding another sign, despite the existing signs being equal in their evidence for the Creator and His perfect attributes.
rows.anchor: عجب منهم عجبا آخر في طلبهم إنزال الآيات مع كونها متساوية الأقدام في الدلالة على الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rejection of the signs already given makes them liable to reject any further signs as well.
rows.anchor: فلما كفروا بما أتاهم كانوا جديرين بالكفر بما يأتيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet longed to satisfy their requests in hope of their faith, but God defines his role as warning through revelation, not implanting faith in hearts.
rows.anchor: الني صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم راغبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A warner is a prophet who explains revelation and alerts people to what leads to ruin or salvation; warning originally means identifying danger so it can be avoided.
rows.anchor: أصل الإنذار الإعلام بموضع المخافة ليتقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every people sent a prophet has a guide who calls them to sound paths and warns them from error, communicating God's warning and glad tidings with fitting signs.
rows.anchor: أي داع يهديهم إلى مراشدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides people with receptivity through visible signs and leaves astray those disposed to error, even if every sign came to them.
rows.anchor: ويضل من يعلم فيه دواعي الضلال ولو جاءته كل آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of divine guidance echoes the statement that God knows what He created.
rows.anchor: ألا يعلم من خلق وهو اللطيف الخبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assignment of a warner to every community parallels the verse saying that no community lacked a warner.
rows.anchor: وإن من أمة إلا خلا فيها نذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guide-and-warner statement also points to this sūra's declaration that God guides whom He wills and guides the one who turns to Him.
rows.anchor: قل إن الله يضل من يشاء ويهدي إليه من أناب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis: mentioning the warner first implies the guide omitted there, and mentioning the guide second implies the warner omitted there.
rows.anchor: ذكر المنذر أولا يدل على حذفه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the requesters are obstinate rather than seeking guidance, God does not grant their proposed signs; instead He points to familiar acts proving His knowledge and power and the possibility of resurrection.
rows.anchor: يقرر من أفعاله المحسوسة لهم المقتضية لاتصافه من العلم والقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If resurrection seems impossible, it is like the first creation; distinguishing a creature's dust after it scatters is less astonishing than distinguishing reproductive fluid from other mixed water.
rows.anchor: تمييز التراب الذي كان منه الحيوان

words: ٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge is eternal in pre-eternity and its relation to particular events renews as those events occur.
rows.anchor: علما قديما في الأزل بما سيوجد وعلما يتجدد تعلقه بحسب حدوث الحادثات على الاستمرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What each female carries is the fluid in her womb capable of becoming a pregnancy.
rows.anchor: الماء الذي يصلح لأن يكون حملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wombs' decrease is the absorption and disappearance of fluid that cannot produce a child.
rows.anchor: فتنشفه فيضمحل لعدم صلاحيته لأن يكون منه ولد

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī defines ghayḍ as a liquid's retreat into a deep, obscure place, and says the verb can be transitive or intransitive.
rows.anchor: كما قال الرماني : ذهاب المائع في العمق الغامض , وفعله متعد لازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wombs may add further fluid and produce twins or more when another conception occurs after the first pregnancy has begun.
rows.anchor: فيكون توأما فأكثر في جماع آخر بعد حمل الأول

rows.speaker: ابن سينا وغيره من الأطباء
rows.claim: Ibn Sīnā and other physicians explicitly affirmed the possibility of conception occurring again after an initial pregnancy.
rows.anchor: كما صرح بإمكان ذلك ابن سينا وغيره من الأطباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī adds that in his own time a she-ass gave birth to a donkey and a mule.
rows.anchor: وولدت في زماننا أتان حمارا وبغلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything is measured precisely in quality and quantity, neither exceeding nor falling short; God's control of these details demonstrates wisdom.
rows.anchor: وذلك كله يستلزم الحكمة فلذا ختمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains God's nurturing of those who disbelieve in Him through processes they can observe and acknowledge.
rows.anchor: من حيث بين فيها تربيته لهم

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī defines the unseen as what is hidden from every creature and the manifest as what appears to them.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : الغيب : كون الشيء بحيث يخفى عن الحس , والشهادة : كونه بحيث يظهر له

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines greatness as an evident disparity of degree: only God has absolute greatness, while human claims to grandeur diminish people and end in public humiliation at resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام أبو الحسن الحرالي : والكبر : ظهور التفاوت في ظاهر وباهر القدر الذي لا يحتاج إلى فكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is beyond approach in essence, attribute, or action; the reciprocal form intensifies the sense of transcendence.
rows.anchor: من أوج علوه في ذات أو صفة أو فعل

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says transcendence means lying beyond reach by judgment or proof: imagined arguments are refuted by God's decisive proof, and He is exalted in knowledge, judgment, and argument.
rows.anchor: وقال أبوالحسن الحرالي رحمه الله : والتعالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding descriptions are as much as human reason can bear; the truth of God's attributes is absolute greatness and transcendence.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى أن ذلك على ما تحتمله العقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat Ibrāhīm is Meccan and has fifty-two verses.
rows.anchor: سورة إبراهيم مكية - آياتها اثنان وخمسون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala names God as uniquely perfect and without equal, merciful to all creation through a supremely clear Book, and especially gracious to servants He chooses.
rows.anchor: تفرد بالكمال , وعز عن أن يكون له كفو أو مثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's purpose is affirming God's oneness and showing the Book as a complete guide to the path leading to Him; its secrets move creation from one stage to another, signaled by the letter rāʾ.
rows.anchor: مقصود السورة التوحيد , وبيان أن هذا الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's story is the sūra's clearest evidence: it affirms oneness and connects the Book to Abraham's prayer for a messenger among his descendants.
rows.anchor: وأدل ما فيها على هذا المرام قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding sūra ended by saying that no testimony matches the testimony of one who has knowledge of the Book; the Qur'an itself testifies through its inimitable eloquence and knowledge.
rows.anchor: ختم الرعد بأنه لا شهادة تكافىء شهادة من عنده علم الكتاب إشارة إلى أن الكتاب هو الشاهد بإعجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier sūras called the Book wise, firmly composed, detailed, clear, and true; here its indefinite form magnifies it beyond ordinary description.
rows.anchor: تكرر وصفه في سورة يونس وهود ويوسف والرعد بأنه حكيم محكم مفصل مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite Book is an expression of glorification: its greatness exceeds what human minds can describe.
rows.anchor: منكرا تنكير التعظيم فقال : { كتاب } أي عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God revealed it to the Messenger in his people's language so he could explain it to them.
rows.anchor: بما لنا من العظمة { إليك } بلسان قومك لتبين لهم

words: لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book and the Prophet's call bring all people, despite their confusion, out of the many forms of misguidance caused by ignorance into God's single path.
rows.anchor: التي هي أنواع كثيرة من الضلالات التي أدت إليها الجهالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase concerns clarifying the message fully to the Arabs in their own language through decisive arguments, making the way to faith unmistakable.
rows.anchor: قومك لأنه بلسانهم بيانا شافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is likened to light because it protects reason from error on the way to God, as physical light protects sight from losing the road; those guided can then guide others.
rows.anchor: وشبه الإيمان وما أرشد إليه بالنور

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummānī says permission originally means release to act through speech heard by the ear.
rows.anchor: هذا أصله - قاله الرماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is clarified as the path of the Mighty, who is free from deficiency and cannot be challenged or have its travelers harmed without His leave.
rows.anchor: فعز عن أن يدخل أحد صراطه الذي هو ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Praiseworthy possesses every perfection and deserves praise both for Himself and for the blessings by which He nurtures His servants.
rows.anchor: فهو المستحق لجميع المحامد لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read Allāh in the nominative as a new sentence; the other readers use the genitive as a clarifying apposition to the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان في قراءة الباقين بالجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the genitive reading, Allāh is a clarifying apposition because the name functions like a proper name exclusive to the true deity and confirms His oneness.
rows.anchor: لأنه جرى مجرى الأسماء الأعلام لاختصاصه بالمعبود بحق ووصفه بما اقتضى توحيده

words: لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is all-knowing and powerful; everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him, and what is owned cannot be His partner.
rows.anchor: فويل لمن أشرك به شيئا منهما أو فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun and its complement emphasizes God's sole creative ownership and oneness.
rows.anchor: أكد بإعادة الموصول مع صلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage may also imply success, safety, and salvation for whoever follows God's path and leaves disbelief; wail means destruction.
rows.anchor: فوأل ونجاة وسلامة لمن اهتدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wail is a verbal noun meaning destruction, inflected like verbal nouns to establish the reality of destruction, the opposite of salvation.
rows.anchor: ينصب نصب المصادر ثم يرفع رفعها لإفادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers who conceal rational proofs face torment intensified in both pain and force; shidda denotes a combination difficult to disentangle.
rows.anchor: والشدة : تجمع يصعب معه التفكيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing that God created and owns all things, the passage recalls Abraham to expose the descendants' ingratitude, idolatry by imitation of forefathers, and neglect of prayer and gratitude.
rows.anchor: أمره صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم أن يذكروهم بأيام الله عند أبيهم إبراهيم عليه السلام للدلالة على تبديلهم النعمة ظلما منهم وكفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder of God's past favors through Abraham also signals resurrection and the need to disavow idols, even though Abraham was their greatest forefather.
rows.anchor: مشير إلى وجوب براءتهم من الأصنام حيث كان محط حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means, 'Remember for them' the account of God's dealings with Abraham.
rows.anchor: أي واذكر لهم مذكرا بأيام الله خبر إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite 'this city' is Mecca, the place from which the opponents want to expel the Messenger and whose people threaten those granted its blessings.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يريدون إخراج الرسول منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's prayer in this passage came after people had settled in Mecca; his earlier prayer in al-Baqara was made in an empty valley, asking first that it become a town and then that it be secure.
rows.anchor: وكأن هذا الدعاء صدر منه بعد أن سكن الناس مكة وصارت مدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safety means that the inhabitants' lives and property are secure and the soul is at rest from danger.
rows.anchor: وهو سكون النفس إلى زوال الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After asking for bodily and property security, Abraham asks for religious security: turn him and his sons aside from idol worship and place them on another side.
rows.anchor: الأمن من فساد الأموال والأبدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons are Abraham's own male descendants; the mention omits daughters as an indication of male independence, since daughters are dependent.
rows.anchor: أسقط البنات إشارة إلى الاستقلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for lasting separation from worship of idols, an act that would merit the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي عبادة مستمرة تكون موجبة للنار
